title: Fix Leaking Http Channel Objects when Http Client Stats are Disabled

timeline.message:
Fix Leaking Http Channel Objects when Http Client Stats are Disabled

We have to remove the channel from the internal collection of channels when stats are disabled.

Closes #76183
timeline.author: Armin Braun

timeline.body:
We have to remove the channel from the internal collection of channels when stats are disabled.

Closes #76183
Would kind of prefer having the assertion straight after the assignment of `addedOnThisCall`
While we're here, let's add an `assert false : e` in the catch block for good measure rather than just commenting that it doesn't throw.

I think this is ok, `CloseableChannel.closeChannels(..., true)` adds a new close listener to all the channels and I am assuming that the listeners definitely complete in the order in which they were added.

reply.body: Unfortunately turns out this doesn't work because in case the channel is already when the listener is added it will potentially run before queued listeners. Looking into an alternative check ...

hmpf that required some extra complexity https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/76257/commits/f4d5454f1c62371115958bf07695118990b24b59 but it may be well worth it, we shouldn't shut down the even loop before all connections have been closed to begin with I think.

timeline.body: LGTM with a couple of nits

timeline.author: Armin Braun
Armin Braun

timeline.body: Making this depend on the lifecycle and complete `allClientsClosedListener` in multiple places seems a bit ugly, could we use a `RefCounted` with one ref for the transport and one for each open channel?
